item.description: Like a gang of tried-and-true mavericks, Rival Sons march to the beat of their own drum. Their very emergence is inexplicable in the best way. They don’t fit into any era or category, yet their uncompromising spirit might be more necessary today than ever. item.title: DJ Rafe Gomez presents Danceteria REWIND at Porta — Sat Nov 28, 9:00 PM — Porta Montclair
item.description: DJ Rafe Gomez, host of the popular Twitch channel Danceteria REWIND, will present an immersive sonic and visual re-creation of the famed NYC nightclub Danceteria at Porta in Montclair. The free event, which will be the tri-state area’s official debut of Rafe’s multimedia performance, will take place on Saturday, 11/28, 499 Bloomfield Avenue, from 9pm to 1am. Danceteria was a New York hotspot from 1979 to 1986. It was famous for embracing iconic art (Keith Haring worked at the club as a waiter, Kenny Scharf was a member of the performance troupe, and Jean-Michel Basquiat painted murals), video, fashion, and music. It’s also where LL Cool J, the Beastie Boys, RuPaul, Debi Mazar, and Madonna got their starts. This year, Danceteria has been trending: Madonna released a #1 hit single titled “Danceteria” that chronicled her adventures there, and the UK synth duo Soft Cell’s new album “Danceteria” explores the early 80s downtown NYC scene that inspired their musical journey. item.title: Everything Book Club, "Life & Death & Giants" by Ron Rindo — Tue Dec 8, 1:15 PM — Montclair Main - Teen Room
item.description:
An American tall tale with a surprising plot and the heart of a giant. Gabriel Fisher is born an orphan, weighing 18 pounds and measuring 27 inches long. Gabriel gets taken in by his devout Amish grandparents who try to protect him from the "English" world. But it’s hard to hide when you’re nearly 8 feet tall. When Gabriel reaches 17, the local football coach spots him tossing hay bales like sofa cushions. What happens next transforms not only Gabriel’s life but the lives of everyone he meets.
"'Life, and Death, and Giants' is an intriguing and alluring novel from beginning to end....Reading it is like meeting a family that you never knew existed and becoming close friends in a few weeks. Highly recommended." --Jane Smiley
RON RINDO is a professor of English and creative writing at the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh. He has published one previous novel, "Breathing Lake Superior, "and three short story collections. He lives in Pickett, Wisconsin.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306
